text:
Situation: Verapamil hydrochloride tablets are not on FDA's drug shortage list as of 2026-10-21. Pfizer Inc.'s verapamil hydrochloride injection entry is marked To Be Discontinued with an initial posting date of 2025-11-21. Corvale East holds 209 tablets of the 120 mg presentation at 9.5 tablets per day, giving 21.9 days on hand. Corvale General holds 442 tablets of the 120 mg presentation at 14.1 tablets per day, giving 31.4 days on hand.

Why (FDA record): FDA's drug shortage list shows verapamil hydrochloride is not listed as of 2026-10-21. A Pfizer Inc. verapamil hydrochloride injection entry is marked To Be Discontinued with an initial posting date of 2025-11-21.

Our position: Tablet inventory provides 21.9 to 31.4 days of supply. No tablet presentations are on FDA's shortage list. Pfizer's discontinuation applies to injection only. Ranked manufacturers are not on FDA's shortage list today, but their labels name no identifiable plant.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to verify current contract terms and allocation limits with Actavis Pharma, Inc. before placing orders; requires P&T Committee approval.
2. Buyer to evaluate AvKARE, Cadila Pharmaceuticals Limited, Chartwell RX, LLC, and Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Inc., USA as secondary sources if Actavis supply is insufficient; requires P&T Committee approval.
3. Buyer to monitor FDA shortage list and Pfizer discontinuation updates weekly; requires Pharmacy Director approval.

Not recommended: Switching to alternative calcium channel blockers or changing verapamil dosing regimens.
